title: Farside: Space Travel Sound Effects
shortText: 121 space SFX: 4 jump drives x 5 phases, docking, planetfall, thrusters, hull impacts, 10 loops. WAV + OGG.
html:
The space journey, as one sound

121 space and sci fi sound effects in WAV and OGG for any game engine (Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and HTML5): 4 complete jump drives (a heavy jump drive, a warp bubble, a ring jump gate and a fold drive), each with spool up, a charge in three rungs, the jump, a seamless transit loop, drop out, misjump and cooldown; docking from the approach beacon to a hard seal; planetfall from atmospheric entry to touchdown on 4 surfaces; navigation with 8 manoeuvring thruster takes; asteroid impacts at four sizes and the hull hazards around them; and mag boots, tether and suit for a spacewalk. Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. A free demo of 19 sounds is on this page.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 19 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The jump drive in every phase with its three charge rungs and its transit loop, the jump align lock, docking in every state from first contact to the push off, and two asteroid impacts on the hull, a small rock and a boulder.

Finished events, not layers

Every sound plays as delivered: named by stage and chained the way a game fires it, with no layering or post processing needed. Space is silent, so every space event here is heard the way a crew hears it, carried through the hull into a small cockpit. The cockpit's own cues are close and nearly dry, planetfall ends on the ground in open air, and a spacewalk is heard inside the helmet. One hull, one sound, from the first spool to the last touchdown.

Four drives, every phase

  • Jump drive: a heavy drive: a deep spool under a thin capacitor whine, one hard snap through, the hull settling after.
  • Warp bubble: a field that swells around the hull and carries the ship forward on one long smooth rise.
  • Jump gate: a ring gate outside the ship: segments locking, the aperture opening, a pressure wave throwing the ship through.
  • Fold drive: a blink drive: space pulled shut in an instant, a short bright tear and the ship elsewhere.

Each drive ships a spool up, a jump, a drop out, a misjump and a cooldown, plus its own charge in three rungs (each brighter than the last) and a seamless transit loop, so a game can give every ship class its own drive and wire every stage of it. Checked from the shipped files, not promised: across the drive by phase grid the drive changes the sound and so does the phase (70 pairs, 0 alike). Wiring it is one string: jump_drive_spool, warp_bubble_jump, fold_drive_charge_3.

Whole lifecycles

  • Docking: contact, clamp engage, hard seal, equalise (loop), umbilical connect, undock release, push off
  • Landing gear: down, lock, up
  • Autopilot: engage, disengage
  • Navigation target: acquire, lock, lost
  • Interdiction: pull, break free
  • Mag boots: clamp, release
  • Tether: clip, release

No two states of one mechanism are the same sound renamed (31 pairs measured from the shipped files, 0 alike).

Ladders a game can wire to its own numbers

The four drive charges, the docking beacon at four ranges, the collision warning at three, atmospheric entry as three crossfading loops (light, heavy, peak heating), and rock striking the hull at four sizes from grit to a boulder, two takes each. 18 ladder steps measured from the shipped files, failing steps: 0.

The rest of the journey

  • 6 jump control sounds: the align lock, countdown tick takes, a jump abort, and an interdiction pull with the break free.
  • 15 docking sounds: the approach beacon ladder, guidance correction pulses (two takes), clearance granted and denied, and the docking lifecycle with pressure equalising as a loop.
  • 18 planetfall sounds: three entry roar loops and a plasma crackle loop, heat shield strain (two takes), a sonic boom, the drogue, a retro burn, landing gear down, locked and up, touchdown on rock, sand, ice and a landing pad, liftoff and the breakout as the air thins away.
  • 19 navigation sounds: 8 manoeuvring thruster takes from a short tap to a long burn, a target acquired, locked and lost, a waypoint, a course plotted, a star fix, the autopilot engaging and letting go, and a three range collision warning.
  • 16 hull hazards: a micrometeorite patter loop, asteroid impacts at four sizes (two takes each), hull stress groans and debris scrapes (two takes each), a hull breach, decompression and a hull patch sealing.
  • 11 spacewalk sounds: mag boots clamping (three takes) and releasing (two), pushing off in zero g (two), a tether clipped and released, the suit sealing and the visor locking.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by group.
  • 10 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 13 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.19 dB, so a boulder on the hull and a waypoint click share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1110 checks, 0 failed.

Already own our other sound packs?

Every file here was measured against every file in the studio's 6 nearest packs (the inside of a spaceship, elemental casting, weather, robots and mechs, natural disasters and footsteps: 139029 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 139029 of 139029 are separate sounds. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds designed for games, not recordings of a real spacecraft: titanium, carbon composite, ceramic tile, steel, aluminium, glass, rubber, rock and ice, air, plasma and field noise. There are no main engine loops, weapons, shields or cockpit menus here; this pack is the journey between places. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. There are no voices and no music: no radio chatter, no announcer, no score.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover is an AI generated illustration, and the store plates are drawn by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Ship Systems, the inside of the ship: interface, reactor, engines, shields and the airlock.
  • Deep Space, a sci fi space music pack, for the score these sounds play under.
  • Servo, robots and mechs, for the crew that is not human.
  • Barrage, shmup and bullet hell sounds, for when the trip turns into a fight.
  • Footfall, footsteps on twelve surfaces, for the walk from the airlock to the bridge.
  • Upheaval, natural disasters, for the planet you land on.
